scope: Primary-source supportive care, longitudinal monitoring and trial-family fit for 16 selected NCCP regimens. This is research input, not independent consultant or pharmacy approval.
source_hierarchy: The current NCCP regimen governs Irish protocol identity, dosing, indication and explicit required monitoring. International guidelines add clearly attributed risk-based longitudinal context; they must not silently replace a stricter NCCP schedule. Trials support their studied population and schedule, not every regimen sharing ingredients.
critical_findings: NCCP NCIS antiemetics v8 is dated 10 February 2025. Its AC high-risk row differs from both generic high-risk and carboplatin AUC>=4 high-risk rows. Do not use one high-risk prescription for all three.

AC-to-taxane regimens need separate antiemetic plans for each phase. Trastuzumab-only continuation is a further minimal-risk phase; cytotoxic premedication and G-CSF must not carry over automatically.
Weekly paclitaxel and q14-day paclitaxel have different suggested steroid premedication tables in current NCCP sources. Day 8 means the next weekly paclitaxel dose, not day 8 of an AC course.

Docetaxel dexamethasone prevents fluid retention and hypersensitivity. It must be reconciled with antiemetic dexamethasone and aprepitant interactions instead of automatically added to a second steroid script.

For sequential AC-to-trastuzumab treatment, show cardiac assessment before AC and reassessment before first trastuzumab. The HER2 monitoring clock starts at first HER2 exposure, not at the start of AC.

Every 12 weeks in NCCP is not mathematically identical to every three calendar months. For illustrative uninterrupted schedules, 12 weeks corresponds to q21-day cycle 5, q14-day cycle 7 or weekly dose 13. The clinical due date remains anchored to elapsed time and may precede a delayed cycle.

Six-monthly metastatic HER2 echo monitoring is a selected stable-patient option after the first year in ESC guidance, not an automatic switch when cytotoxic chemotherapy stops. NCCP/SmPC schedules and the treating team's plan still govern.

An updated 2026 ESMO metastatic breast guideline was found. It still supports individualized assessment every 2-4 months. Avoid declaring historical THP universally the latest preferred first-line option; preserve the exact current NCCP indication.

00203 and 00621 have multi-tumour indications. Breast-specific mammography, endocrine and surgery pathways must remain conditional on the selected breast indication; do not overwrite other tumour contexts.

00512 explicitly allows weekly or q21-day trastuzumab continuation to complete one year. Its reference to weekly monotherapy 00201 must not switch an early adjuvant patient into the metastatic-labelled standalone portal.

No exact randomized evidence match was established for 00621 paclitaxel days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days in this bounded review. Do not label E1199 or APT as direct evidence for that advanced-disease schedule.

TRYPHAENA used intravenous trastuzumab. For 00731, distinguish evidence for the TCHP chemotherapy strategy from evidence supporting subcutaneous trastuzumab formulation. Do not represent TRYPHAENA numerical results as a separate SC-regimen trial.

guidelines.title: NCCP Supportive Care Antiemetic Medicines for inclusion in NCIS (Medical Oncology)
guidelines.location: Table 1, PDF p4; steroid-reconciliation note p5
guidelines.verified_summary: AC: day 1 aprepitant 125 mg, ondansetron 16 mg, dexamethasone 12 mg and olanzapine 5 mg orally; later aprepitant 80 mg days 2-3 and olanzapine 5 mg days 2-4. Its row does not include routine delayed dexamethasone. Carboplatin AUC>=4: aprepitant/ondansetron/dexamethasone, with aprepitant days 2-3 and dexamethasone days 2-4; routine olanzapine is not in this row. Moderate-risk therapy uses ondansetron/dexamethasone; low-risk default is ondansetron 8 mg day 1 with PRN metoclopramide. Existing regimen steroids may require dexamethasone modification/omission. Local alternatives and patient-specific changes are permitted. Ondansetron QT risk and additive extrapyramidal risk with olanzapine/metoclopramide require review.
guidelines.implementation_limit: Draft prescriptions require local pharmacy reconciliation; the shared risk band alone does not establish a complete individualized prescription. Separate rows must remain distinguishable.

guidelines.title: 2022 ESC Guidelines on cardio-oncology
guidelines.verified_summary: Baseline clinical cardiovascular assessment and ECG apply to all patients. Echo is recommended before anthracyclines and HER2 therapy. Anthracycline surveillance depends on baseline risk and cumulative exposure: high/very-high risk merits echo every two cycles and within three months afterwards; all adults need echo within 12 months after completion. In lower risk, additional imaging/biomarkers depend partly on cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent dose, including 250 mg/m². HER2 surveillance is generally every three months during early treatment and the first metastatic year. Selected asymptomatic low/moderate-risk metastatic patients with normal assessment may move to six-monthly echo after year one; high-risk metastatic patients may need checks every 2-3 cycles.
guidelines.implementation_limit: A single universal anthracycline echo cycle is inappropriate. Label risk-based checks and do not relax NCCP monitoring automatically. Four AC 60 mg/m² doses total 240 mg/m², but previous anthracycline exposure and patient risk remain relevant.
guidelines.access_note: Official publisher search excerpts verified; direct fulltext fetch returned 403. ESC's own 2023 implementation article was also read.

guidelines.title: ESC CardioPractice: Monitoring and treatment of cardiovascular complications during cancer therapies, Part I
guidelines.verified_summary: ESC describes tailored surveillance integrating clinical review, troponin/natriuretic peptides and echo with LVEF/strain according to baseline cardiovascular risk. It stresses that cardiac injury can be asymptomatic and that post-anthracycline assessments at six and/or 12 months should be considered.
guidelines.implementation_limit: This explains why the timeline includes symptom-independent checks. It is an official educational implementation article, not a new independent 2023 guideline.

guidelines.title: Roche Herceptin 150 mg SmPC
guidelines.location: Section 4.4, cardiac dysfunction / early breast cancer
guidelines.verified_summary: Baseline cardiac assessment includes clinical evaluation, ECG and cardiac imaging. During treatment, cardiac assessments repeat every three months. In early breast cancer, assessment continues every six months after stopping until 24 months after the final dose. Patients previously given anthracyclines can need additional longer follow-up. Intravenous and subcutaneous trastuzumab formulations have distinct administration requirements; trastuzumab, T-DM1 and trastuzumab deruxtecan are not interchangeable names.
guidelines.implementation_limit: Primary manufacturer UK SmPC used as corroboration; the Irish NCCP protocol and applicable Irish/EU product information govern local care. Current EMA URL returned a rate-limit response during this lookup.

guidelines.title: Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for early breast cancer
guidelines.verified_summary: Annual bilateral mammography after breast conservation or contralateral mammography after mastectomy is recommended, with additional breast imaging when indicated. Routine non-breast imaging or laboratory/tumour-marker surveillance is not recommended for asymptomatic relapse detection. New symptoms warrant directed investigation. Bone density evaluation applies to aromatase inhibitors or ovarian suppression. HER2 therapy may overlap indicated radiotherapy and endocrine treatment. Dose-dense chemotherapy should include G-CSF support.
guidelines.implementation_limit: These follow-up recommendations do not replace treatment-toxicity blood tests during SACT. A patient can therefore need routine FBC/LFT monitoring while not needing routine CT/CA15-3 surveillance. Radiotherapy, endocrine treatment and mastectomy are conditional, not mandatory next steps for every patient.
guidelines.access_note: Full PMC text retrieved by standard public HTTP and saved in early2024.txt; web-open encountered a browser check. Adaptation is based on the 2023/2024 ESMO early-breast guideline.

guidelines.title: Metastatic breast cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up
guidelines.verified_summary: Baseline staging can use chest/abdominal CT plus bone scintigraphy, or FDG-PET-CT. The guideline recommends no more than four weeks between baseline imaging and treatment initiation, and a consistent modality for comparison. Response assessment may occur every 2-4 months according to symptoms, disease dynamics, distribution and treatment. Routine shortening of intervals lacks proven survival benefit and can cause harm.
guidelines.implementation_limit: Patient text should say an agreed response scan, often about 2-4 months, with earlier review for new symptoms. Do not hard-code CT thorax/abdomen/pelvis every three months for every cancer or every breast setting. A cycle annotation must specify the actual cycle length.
guidelines.access_note: Verified current publisher-indexed passage; direct fulltext returned 403, so no additional 2026 recommendations were inferred from inaccessible sections.

guidelines.title: 5th ESO-ESMO international consensus guidelines for advanced breast cancer (ABC 5)
guidelines.verified_summary: Elevated tumour markers can supplement response assessment, especially in non-measurable metastatic disease, but a marker rise alone must not determine a treatment change. Historical practical monitoring guidance is every 2-4 months for endocrine treatment or after 2-4 chemotherapy cycles, individualized by disease and treatment; suspected progression prompts assessment outside scheduled intervals.
guidelines.implementation_limit: Retain this specific marker limitation with attribution to ABC5. A fixed 'every 2-4 cycles' label is ambiguous for weekly regimens and must not replace current time-based ESMO guidance.

guidelines.title: NICE NG101: Early and locally advanced breast cancer, bone health
guidelines.version_date: Live recommendations checked 2026-10-17; relevant bone recommendation amended 2018
guidelines.verified_summary: Baseline DEXA is linked to treatment-associated bone risk, including starting adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy, induced menopause or ovarian suppression; the recommendation distinguishes patients already receiving adjuvant bisphosphonates. Bone mineral density assessment also applies when testicular suppression is combined with an aromatase inhibitor. Bone assessment is not a universal scan simply because someone receives chemotherapy.
guidelines.implementation_limit: Use conditional baseline DEXA/bone-risk language. Repeat interval should follow baseline result, risk and bone-protection plan; do not invent a universal yearly scan.

guidelines.title: NCI Breast Cancer Treatment PDQ: Timing of postoperative radiation therapy
guidelines.verified_summary: Evidence supports completing adjuvant chemotherapy before postoperative breast radiotherapy without loss of overall outcome from that sequencing. Concurrent adjuvant trastuzumab and radiotherapy appears feasible in the cited trial analyses.
guidelines.implementation_limit: Draw separate illustrative pathways: surgery -> adjuvant cytotoxic chemotherapy -> indicated RT, versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy -> surgery/pathology -> indicated RT/postoperative systemic treatment. Show possible HER2/endocrine overlap with RT rather than implying every therapy must finish first. Local MDT decisions determine surgery, RT indication and timing.

premedication_families.source_basis: Current NCCP PDFs already downloaded in v0840-sources; supportive-care tables reviewed for each listed code.
premedication_families.summary: Suggested first-dose premedication: dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV 30 minutes before paclitaxel. Subsequent weekly doses list no dexamethasone when no hypersensitivity reaction has occurred; antihistamine/H2 policies and consultant footnotes apply. Previous reactions require a separate plan; do not encode unsupervised steroid cessation.
premedication_families.phase_note: Antiemesis is low risk; this premedication is primarily reaction prevention. A low-risk antiemetic script does not replace the taxane premedication plan.

premedication_families.summary: The q14-day suggested table uses dexamethasone 20 mg orally at approximately 12 and six hours before treatment, or IV 30 minutes before; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV are listed. Reduction/omission requires consultant guidance. The source notes consideration of dexamethasone reduction to 12 mg on treatment day if aprepitant is added.
premedication_families.phase_note: Do not substitute the weekly first-dose-only dexamethasone table. Keep the AC high-risk antiemetic phase separate.

premedication_families.summary: Dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice daily for three days starting the day before docetaxel, with at least three pre-treatment doses, unless contraindicated. A consultant may consider the source's IV alternative after missed oral doses. This reduces fluid retention and hypersensitivity; do not tell patients to improvise a missed-dose replacement.
premedication_families.phase_note: Low-risk single-agent docetaxel/THP, moderate-risk TC, and high-risk carboplatin-containing TCH(P) have different antiemetic support despite sharing docetaxel. Avoid duplicate dexamethasone.

premedication_families.summary: Antibody premedication is not usually required without a previous reaction; reaction history can prompt paracetamol/antihistamine cover and observation planning. Do not retain docetaxel/paclitaxel steroids, cytotoxic antiemetics or G-CSF automatically after the cytotoxic component stops.
premedication_families.phase_note: Only describe a continuation strategy actually authorized by the source/treatment plan. After neoadjuvant HER2 therapy, surgical pathology determines the next systemic phase; do not promise every patient the same continuation drug.

trial_sources.title: NSABP B-15: AC versus CMF
trial_sources.summary: Historical adjuvant trial comparing a short AC course with six months of CMF in node-positive, tamoxifen-nonresponsive disease.
trial_sources.limit: Historical regimen rationale only; not a modern individualized absolute-benefit estimate or evidence that AC alone is preferred across every breast subtype.

trial_sources.title: CALGB 9741 / Intergroup C9741 dose-density trial
trial_sources.summary: Randomized factorial trial in postoperative node-positive breast cancer comparing sequential/concurrent AC-taxane strategies and two-weekly versus three-weekly scheduling, with growth-factor support for dose-dense treatment.
trial_sources.limit: Supports dose-density rationale. It did not test adding trastuzumab or all weekly-taxane/HER2 schedules, and it was not a neoadjuvant trial. Do not transplant numerical results into those cards.

trial_sources.title: E1199: Weekly paclitaxel in adjuvant breast cancer
trial_sources.summary: After standard AC, patients with node-positive or high-risk node-negative operable breast cancer received different taxanes/schedules; weekly paclitaxel improved outcomes relative to the reference three-weekly paclitaxel arm.
trial_sources.limit: Adjuvant AC followed by weekly paclitaxel evidence, not direct evidence for advanced paclitaxel days 1/8/15 every 28 days, trastuzumab addition, or every dose-dense AC variant.

trial_sources.title: NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831: Trastuzumab plus adjuvant chemotherapy
trial_sources.summary: These adjuvant trials tested adding trastuzumab to AC followed by paclitaxel in operable HER2-positive breast cancer.
trial_sources.limit: Supports the AC-taxane-HER2 strategy; dose-dense variants, q21-day trastuzumab substitutions and neoadjuvant indications require their own NCCP/context attribution. Not evidence for concurrent AC and trastuzumab.

trial_sources.title: Harvey et al: Three doses of docetaxel in second-line advanced breast cancer
trial_sources.summary: Randomized docetaxel 60, 75 and 100 mg/m² every three weeks in patients with previously treated advanced breast cancer.
trial_sources.limit: Provides breast-specific dose/schedule evidence, not evidence for 00203's prostate, lung, gastric or gynaecological indications. Do not transfer one dose arm's numeric efficacy or toxicity to another.

trial_sources.title: US Oncology 9735: TC versus AC, seven-year follow-up
trial_sources.summary: Randomized four q21-day cycles of TC 75/600 versus four cycles of AC 60/600 after complete surgery for stage I-III operable breast cancer.
trial_sources.limit: The comparison was AC alone, not a modern anthracycline-taxane sequence. Four-cycle findings must not be relabelled as direct six-cycle TC evidence.

trial_sources.title: APT: Final 10-year analysis
trial_sources.summary: Open-label single-arm phase II study of 12 weeks of weekly paclitaxel plus trastuzumab, followed by trastuzumab to complete one year, for small node-negative HER2-positive breast cancer.
trial_sources.limit: No randomized untreated control. The studied low-risk adjuvant population differs from node-positive, neoadjuvant and metastatic populations. Do not use an APT survival percentage as an individual prognosis or apply it to other taxane schedules.

trial_sources.title: BCIRG 006: Adjuvant trastuzumab in HER2-positive breast cancer
trial_sources.summary: Randomized HER2-positive early breast cancer to AC-docetaxel, AC-docetaxel plus trastuzumab, or six cycles of docetaxel/carboplatin/trastuzumab with trastuzumab continued for one year.
trial_sources.limit: Supports adjuvant TCH. It did not test pertuzumab, neoadjuvant TCHP, or SC trastuzumab as a separate efficacy comparison; absence of a significant difference between active arms is not proof of equivalence.

trial_sources.title: TRYPHAENA: Neoadjuvant pertuzumab/trastuzumab with chemotherapy
trial_sources.summary: Randomized phase II cardiac-safety study of three neoadjuvant strategies in HER2-positive operable, locally advanced or inflammatory breast cancer. Arm C used six q3-week cycles of docetaxel/carboplatin with IV trastuzumab and pertuzumab, followed by surgery and trastuzumab to one year.
trial_sources.limit: A cardiac-safety phase II study with differing pCR definitions, not a definitive survival trial. 00731 uses SC trastuzumab: describe the formulation bridge separately, and do not label an IV trial result as directly measured SC-regimen efficacy.

trial_sources.title: CLEOPATRA: End-of-study analysis
trial_sources.summary: Double-blind randomized phase III study of pertuzumab versus placebo with trastuzumab and docetaxel in previously untreated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer.
trial_sources.limit: Direct docetaxel/IV-antibody metastatic evidence. It does not supply numerical outcomes for weekly paclitaxel substitution, neoadjuvant TCHP or SC formulations. Historical efficacy does not establish today's reimbursed preferred sequence.

trial_sources.title: Weekly paclitaxel with trastuzumab and pertuzumab: Five-year follow-up
trial_sources.summary: Phase II study of paclitaxel 80 mg/m² weekly with q21-day IV trastuzumab and pertuzumab in HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer with zero or one previous metastatic treatment.
trial_sources.limit: Single-arm phase II evidence; not a randomized equivalence comparison against docetaxel. Do not copy CLEOPATRA survival estimates into this card.

family_monitoring_map.AC_and_AC_taxane_00252_00260_00278: Baseline clinical review/ECG/echo and protocol bloods -> phase-specific AC and taxane blood/toxicity checks -> risk-based cardiac reassessment -> surgery/pathology if neoadjuvant OR prior surgery if adjuvant -> indicated RT -> HR-dependent endocrine/bone plan -> annual breast imaging and symptom-directed follow-up.
family_monitoring_map.AC_taxane_HER2_00316_00432_00433_00745: Add reassessment before first trastuzumab after AC, then time-based HER2 echo checks across taxane and antibody-only phases. Record HER2 start separately from AC start. Show post-treatment cardiac follow-up and possible RT/endocrine overlap.
family_monitoring_map.TC_00250: Adjuvant pathway after surgery, bloods before each cycle, pre-docetaxel steroid start day -1. No automatic anthracycline/HER2 echo schedule; baseline clinical CV risk can still warrant ECG/other assessment. RT/endocrine/DEXA remain conditional.
family_monitoring_map.APT_00512: After surgery: 12 weekly paclitaxel/H doses -> trastuzumab-only completion of one year. Echo baseline and every 12 weeks per NCCP; first repeat near transition to continuation. RT can overlap antibody continuation; endocrine only if HR-positive.
family_monitoring_map.TCH_00258: Adjuvant six-cycle cytotoxic/HER2 phase -> antibody continuation. Echo baseline and every 12 weeks across both phases, first repeat around cycle 5 on an uninterrupted q21-day schedule. Separate cytotoxic bloods/premeds from continuation.
family_monitoring_map.TCH_SC_P_00731: Neoadjuvant treatment -> response assessment for surgery -> surgery/pathology -> postoperative systemic and RT plan. Do not preassign residual-disease treatment before pathology. Keep separate SC trastuzumab and IV pertuzumab identities.
family_monitoring_map.advanced_docetaxel_paclitaxel_00202_0020: Baseline disease imaging and protocol bloods -> blood/toxicity review at the source interval -> agreed response imaging usually 2-4 months for breast indication -> continue/change according to response and tolerance. No fixed completion surgery or annual mammography pathway for metastatic disease.
family_monitoring_map.metastatic_THP_00204_00507: Baseline HER2 cardiac/disease assessment -> taxane plus antibodies with timed echo/scan reviews -> possible antibody maintenance after taxane stops. Monitoring continues during maintenance; a switch to six-monthly echo requires the selected stable-risk context and an explicit clinical plan.

review_limits: No patient-specific treatment recommendation was made.
Exact NCCP blood thresholds, dose modifications, dose omissions and indications are the remit of the separate regimen audits; shared sources must not overwrite them.
The 2026 ESMO publisher fulltext was inaccessible directly; only the publicly indexed staging/monitoring passage was used.
Numeric trial outcomes were intentionally not copied into the family map; each card needs exact endpoint, timepoint, population, comparison and route/schedule if figures are later included.
Source checking is not independent clinical validation. Consultant/pharmacy/PPI review remains pending.
